title: eGurukul · Spleen
deckName: created by tele @Neet_pg_bot::eguru::q banks::surgery e qb::Spleen

questions.stem: A 53-year-old male presented with a history of post-prandial fullness of the abdomen. CT scan revealed a retroperitoneal mass with intra-abdominal extension. Perioperatively there was a large mesenteric tumor infiltrating the greater omentum. Tumor was resected. There was a gray-brown/tan nodule in the omentum measuring 2x 1cm. On Microscopic examination, the Gray brown nodule in the omentum showed a well-formed capsule, trabeculae, red pulp, and white pulp of the spleen and was diagnosed as splenunculi. The most common site for splenunculi in descending order of frequency is:

options.label: A
options.text: Gastrocolic Ligament, the Pancreatic Tail, the Greater Omentum.

options.label: B
options.text: Gastrocolic Ligament, the Greater Omentum, Hilum of the Spleen.

options.label: C
options.text: Hilum of the Spleen, the Greater Omentum, the Pancreatic Tail

options.label: D
options.text: Hilum of the Spleen, the Pancreatic Tail, the Greater Omentum
